correctness.rationale: Theorem 3.15 in Bonzio–Pra Baldi 2023 forces a strictly descending sequence of finite Boolean intervals along an index chain. Cardinality is a sum of distinct powers of two. Conversely nested subset supports yield surjective restriction homomorphisms and interval isomorphisms satisfying their Theorem 3.17. The unique binary expansion fixes the support-size profile and a base-atom permutation matches any two such profiles. The automorphism action has no index permutations, and the stabilizer of the support chain is exactly the product of the symmetric groups on successive differences. The rigid-size formula follows from each factor having degree at most one. verify.py returns VERIFY_OK 15154351 and VERIFY_AXIOMS_OK 156475.

value.rationale: Finite linearly indexed Płonka algebras are a natural enumeration problem studied for IBSL in 2018, where fine spectra require nontrivial algorithms. The Bochvar external operations collapse the entire finite chain-index census to a single isomorphism type at each positive size, and determine the automorphism group and exact rigidity positions directly from binary digits. This gives complete natural finite isomorphism and symmetry invariants; the proof is short but the combined classification is motivated and not a fabricated arbitrary slice.
